title: Beauty and teaching evaluations
subtitle: Real course data, nothing planted. A published finding, tested blind.
question: Do instructors rated as better-looking receive higher course teaching evaluations?

decision_rule.metric: effect of the instructor's beauty rating on the course evaluation score (1-5 scale) per unit of the beauty rating

story: 463 courses taught at the University of Texas at Austin in 2000-2002, with the average student evaluation of each course and a beauty rating of its instructor from a panel of six students. A published study reported that better-looking instructors get better evaluations. Real data, nothing planted; a live run only.

column_notes.minority: does the instructor belong to a minority (non-Caucasian)?
column_notes.credits: is the course a single-credit elective (e.g., yoga, aerobics, dance)?
column_notes.beauty: rating of the instructor's physical appearance by a panel of six students, averaged across the six panelists, shifted to have a mean of zero; the exposure of interest
column_notes.eval: course overall teaching evaluation score, on a scale of 1 (very unsatisfactory) to 5 (excellent); the outcome
column_notes.division: is the course an upper or lower division course? (lower division courses are mainly large freshman and sophomore courses)
column_notes.native: is the instructor a native English speaker?
column_notes.tenure: is the instructor on tenure track?
column_notes.students: number of students that participated in the evaluation
column_notes.allstudents: number of students enrolled in the course
